# Technologies for Artificial Intelligence — the core environment
#
# Deliberately free of any LLM stack: this course covers ML fundamentals and
# nothing here requires an API key or a network call at runtime. No notebook in
# the course fetches data; every dataset is either a scikit-learn built-in or is
# generated by the lesson's own module.
#
# ============================
# Why every version is pinned
# ============================
# Each notebook opens with a commented `# pip install ...` line naming exact
# versions, and tools/verify_lesson.py compares those names against what the
# image actually ships. Before these pins existed the match was luck: a rebuild
# would have installed numpy 2.x and failed verification on all ten lessons.
# Change a version here and the notebooks' pip lines must change with it.
#
# ============================
# What is deliberately absent
# ============================
# JupyterLab, ipykernel and the notebook server come from the base image, which
# ships JupyterLab 4.2.5. Installing them again here is precisely what produced
# a duplicated layer in the previous build, worth over a gigabyte.
#
# Also absent, having been checked against every import in every notebook and
# helper module: seaborn, statsmodels, xgboost, graphviz, pooch, tensorboard,
# ipywidgets, ipympl. None of them is imported anywhere in the course.
#
# TensorFlow is not here either. It is needed by lessons 9 and 10 alone, it
# weighs 1.3 GB, and it lives in requirements-full.txt so that students are not
# asked to download it in September to use it in November.

numpy==1.26.4
pandas==2.1.1
scipy==1.11.3
matplotlib==3.8.0
scikit-learn==1.3.1
